svg.title: Glyphosate in the border villages
svg.desc: The southern border strip of Lebanon from Ras al-Naqoura to Ayta ash-Shaab: the soil and herb sampling sites of CNRS-L and the Lebanese Army after the herbicide spraying of 1 February 2026, and the land CNRS-L estimates was affected in ten communities (2,122 ha in its table), each a circle whose area is in proportion to its hectares.
svg.text: After the herbicide spraying of 1 February
2026: the land affected per community, and
Its table lists 2,122 ha in ten communities; the
directly or indirectly along the border strip.
Village lands named in the zone from 18
Lebanon's boundary; in the south, the
at 0 to 5 and 5 to 25 cm, and
Clean zone, as the report names
Codes as printed: HZ hot zone, CZ clean
zone; A Ayta ash-Shaab, N Ras al-Naqoura,
Each community's circle sits on its gazetteer point, which places the village, not the land affected: the report gives no sprayed area in coordinates. Borj
an-Naqoura is drawn at An-Naqoura and Mazraat az-Zalloutiyeh at Az-Zalloutiyah; Btayshiyeh, which has no gazetteer point, inside its approximate territory.
Ramyeh's 201 ha include an olive row of 29 ha that the table prints with no village name.
* The table prints المروانية (Al-Marwaniyeh), the name of a town in Sidon district 39 km to the north. The report's own map of the sampling sites names
Marouahine (Marwahin) in this strip and no Marwaniyeh, so its 401 ha are drawn at Marwahin.
Sampling sites at the coordinates the report prints, read as UTM zone 36N (it prints no datum, zone or projection). Ras al-Naqoura's four hot zone sites lie
within 129 m of one another, and its clean zone CZ.N.1 is printed with the coordinates of Al-Dhayra's CZ.D.1. The army's samples 774 (Al-Dhayra) and 777
(Ayta ash-Shaab) have no usable position. HZ.A.1 is in the sampling record only, with no result.
Source: CNRS-L, report of 22 May 2026; analyses by the Lebanese Atomic Energy Commission. Boundaries: UN OCHA and Lebanon's Central Administration of Statistics
